name: NE-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+27 partisan lean makes this one of the most Republican districts in the country
Smith holds a roughly 30-to-1 fundraising advantage over Stille
Prediction markets price Smith's win odds near 97 percent

model.rationale: The district's 27-point Republican lean, Smith's overwhelming money advantage, and the absence of any polling, outside spending against him, or expert attention all point to a comfortable incumbent hold, and markets price his chances near 97 percent.
model.watch: A wave-level Democratic environment or a late influx of outside spending against Smith could narrow the margin, though nothing currently suggests the seat is in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nebraska's 3rd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 27 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Adrian Smith is running again with a large financial edge: about $1.8 million raised and $1 million in cash on hand, compared with roughly $55,000 raised by Democrat Becky Stille. No outside groups are spending against Smith, and no public polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets give Smith about a 97 percent chance of winning, and the Democratic challenger's minimal fundraising offers little sign of a serious contest. The national political environment in 2026 leans toward Democrats, but a shift of that size would fall well short of closing a gap this wide. The forecast expects Smith to win comfortably, with the main uncertainty being the size of his margin rather than the outcome.
